deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages). K^1 is a 1-complex subdivided into 'pseudo-lines'. Every vertex lies on at least two pseudo-lines, and two distinct pseudo-lines meet in exactly one vertex. This is an abstract, combinatorial version of an arrangement of pseudolines in the real projective plane. For a pseudo-line D, Omega(D) is evidently its set of two orientations (D is a circle). On the previous page the orientations of D and D' are compared through the order of points on D-{t} and D'-{t}, where t = D∩D'.

The central construction is the perspectivity. Take a vertex s on neither D nor D'. The pseudo-lines Delta_i through s (and not through t) meet D in u_i and D' in u'_i. One declares the orientations of D and D' to correspond when the orders of the u_i and of the u'_i match. This gives a bijection phi_{s;D,D'}: Omega(D) -> Omega(D').

The goal of this page is to show that this bijection is well defined and essentially independent of s. The expected statement, written out on the next page as property (b), is that phi_s depends only on which of the two regions cut out by D∪D' contains s. On a pseudo-line Delta it depends only on which of the two arcs determined by x = Delta∩D and x' = Delta∩D' contains s.

The page carries on a case analysis.
1. If there is an auxiliary pseudo-line D'' avoiding t, u and u', one can transport through D''. One compares Omega(D'') with Omega(D) and Omega(D'') with Omega(D'), deduces the comparison of Omega(D) with Omega(D'), and 'on gagne'.
2. If every pseudo-line not through t passes through u, or every one passes through u', the configuration is two pencils (vertices t and u, resp. t and u'). This 'demande encore un traitement à part' and is deferred.
3. In the remaining case, Gamma avoids u (but passes through u') and Gamma' avoids u' (but passes through u). Then Omega(Gamma) ≃ Omega(D') and Omega(Gamma') ≃ Omega(D). From Omega(Gamma) ≃ Omega(Gamma') one deduces Omega(D) ≃ Omega(D'), provided the intersection r of Gamma and Gamma' does not lie on Delta'.
4. In the bad sub-case the six pseudo-lines D, D', Delta, Delta', Gamma, Gamma' are, as the next page says, the six lines joining pairwise four vertices u, u', v, t. That is a complete quadrangle. There one checks directly that the bijection defined by s coincides with the one defined by v.

The figure shows this configuration: D and D' through t, Delta through u, u' and s, with Delta', Gamma and Gamma'.

The page thus serves an axiomatic, purely combinatorial treatment of pseudoline systems. Perspectivities transport orientations between pseudo-lines, and the dependence on the region of the centre reflects the projective-plane topology.
errors: The argument is a sketch with deferred cases. The two-pencil case is explicitly postponed ('demande encore un traitement à part'), and the complete-quadrangle sub-case is only settled on the next page.

The hypotheses needed for each comparison are left implicit: centres must avoid both pseudo-lines being compared. For example, comparing Omega(Gamma) and Omega(D') needs a suitable centre off Gamma ∪ D'. Plausible, but not checked on the page.
No mathematical error is visible beyond this incompleteness.

ideas.what: Abstract axiomatization of a pseudoline system as a 1-complex in which any two pseudo-lines meet in exactly one vertex
ideas.modern_name: Pseudoline arrangements / rank-3 oriented matroids (topological representation)

ideas.what: Perspectivity from a vertex s inducing a bijection of orientation sets Omega(D) -> Omega(D'), defined via the order of intersection points
ideas.modern_name: Perspectivity / central projection; orientation transport in pseudoline arrangements (related to chirotope sign data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical projective geometry; combinatorial version implicit in oriented matroid theory

ideas.what: Independence of the perspectivity bijection from the centre within each of the two regions cut out by D∪D', proved by transport through auxiliary pseudo-lines and a case analysis ending in a complete-quadrangle configuration
ideas.modern_name: Well-definedness of region-dependent orientation transport (a Z/2-valued comparison reflecting non-orientability of RP^2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not standardly stated in this form; follows from topological representation of arrangements

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a purely combinatorial (1-skeleton only) proof that perspectivities give a consistent, region-dependent identification of orientations of pseudo-lines. The two-pencil degenerate case is explicitly left for separate treatment. As an intrinsic combinatorial derivation, without passing to the topological plane, this is a modest unfinished thread. It is not clearly new relative to oriented matroid theory.
missed.quote: on est dans le cas des deux faisceaux de ps. droites, de sommet t et u (resp. u'), qui demande encore un traitement à part
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with the oriented-matroid derivation of chirotope signs from the face lattice. It is of mainly historical interest as part of Grothendieck's 1980s work on combinatorial geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but elementary case analysis about perspectivities in abstract pseudoline systems. The underlying facts are standard in pseudoline and oriented-matroid theory. Its historical interest is that Grothendieck worked on this in the early 1980s, but the page itself contains no surprising result.
